text:
maria-rt: Quick sync — saw a big tail latency when GPU nodepools scale from zero in eu-west-1 this morning. 90s coldstarts spiking request latency to 3-4s for first tokens. Any ideas beyond the usual warm-pool?
kevin-g: ugh yeah saw that too. warm-pool helps but it's pricey. been prototyping a "ghost pod" pattern — tiny placeholder pods that reserve scheduling bandwidth and keep kube API thinking nodes are used. then swap in GPU pods via rollout.
sam-sre: curious, how do you swap without triggering image pulls / attach delays? node provisioning still the slow part.
jordan-ml: we tried a related approach: keep a cheap cpu-backed DaemonSet with minimal image (<<10MB) on a tiny node pool. when traffic hits, a controller creates a GPU pod with nodeSelector that prefers nodes with the placeholder. avoids scheduling backlog + shortens schedule decision time.
maria-rt: that sounds promising. downside is added complexity + cost of the tiny pool. can we make it autoscale down to 0 and still be useful?
kevin-g: idea: circuit-breaker controller that keeps exactly N placeholders during business hours (N=2 per AZ), scales to 0 off-hours. metric: warm_placeholder_hit_ratio. if ratio < 0.1, kill placeholders.
sam-sre: also check cluster-autoscaler flags, we were losing scale-up signals because CA's `--expendable-pods-priority-cutoff` treated placeholders as expendable and deleted them. patch suggestion: set priorityClass for placeholders above cutoff.
ops-bot: [alert] 1822003501 autoscaler: scale-up triggered for gpu-pool-eu-west-1 (requested 4 -> 8)
jordan-ml: other friction point is PVC binding for model caches. If PVCs are in different storage class or provisioner is slow, pods stay Pending post-schedule. Precreate PVCs or use emptyDir for boot cache.
kevin-g: config snippet we've been testing: ```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
data:
  cluster-autoscaler-args: |
    --scale-down-delay-after-add=10m
    --max-empty-bulk-delete=5
    --expendable-pods-priority-cutoff=-10
```
maria-rt: nice. also consider local image registry mirror in eu-west to avoid 30s+ image pulls. that plus placeholder nodes should push coldstart down to ~25-35s.
sam-sre: region note — ap-southeast spots are flaky; prewarm in a stable instance pool (on-demand) for that region only. cost analysis: placeholder cpu pool adds ~3-4% infra cost but reduces P95 latency spikes and saves customer retries.
jordan-ml: +1 on measuring user-visible cost. propose new metric set: `scale_up_time_90`, `first_token_latency_95`, `warm_placeholder_hit_ratio`, `gpu_idle_seconds_before_drain`.
kevin-g: ops action: I'll hack a PoC controller that creates placeholders with PriorityClass `system-node-critical-lite` and exposes the hit_ratio metric. give me 2 days.
maria-rt: assign kevin-g. sam-sre can you validate CA flags and test PVC prebind workflows?
sam-sre: on it, will run in staging and report by EOD tomorrow.
ops-bot: meeting-scheduler: created event "GPU coldstart mitigation working session" for 2026-07-08 16:00 UTC, invited: maria-rt, kevin-g, sam-sre, jordan-ml
maria-rt: thanks, we'll keep the warm_pool config as a fallback but move forward with the ghost-placeholder PoC. :thumbsup:
